He felt a pinch on his arm where the small mosquito had bitten him during the camping trip yesterday.
explanation: 'in a pinch' = if needed (idiom). Not literal pinching.
explanationJa: 「in a pinch」は「いざという時」。つねる意味ではない。

sentences: She played par for the course at the golf club last Saturday afternoon with her father and her uncle.
Please mark par for the course on the scorecard before you tee off at the first hole this morning.
Late deliveries are pretty much par for the course with them.
He shot par for the course at the championship tournament held at the country club last weekend.
explanation: 'par for the course' = expected (idiom). Not literal golf score.
explanationJa: 「par for the course」は「お決まり/想定内」。ゴルフの得点の意味ではない。

sentences: She gave or took the package from the courier at the front door of the building this morning.
It'll take an hour, give or take, depending on traffic conditions.
Please give or take the box from the storage closet because we need to make some space for the new shipment.
He gave or took the keys to the new tenant at the apartment building near the city center yesterday.
explanation: 'give or take' = approximately (idiom). Not give/take action.
explanationJa: 「give or take」は「だいたい」。「与える/受け取る」意味ではない。

sentences: She saw eye to eye with her doctor during the annual checkup at the clinic this morning early.
Please see eye to eye with the optometrist because she wants to test how well your contact lenses fit now.
He saw eye to eye with the small child at the museum and they smiled at each other for a moment.
We don't always see eye to eye, but we work well together.
explanation: 'see eye to eye' = agree (idiom). Not literal eye contact.
explanationJa: 「see eye to eye」は「意見が合う」。実際の目の意味ではない。

sentences: She kept the letter posted on the refrigerator with a small magnet for nearly three weeks now.
Keep me posted on how the negotiation goes tomorrow.
Please keep the notice posted on the bulletin board until the end of the week because everyone needs to read it.
He kept the photograph posted on his bedroom wall above his desk for nearly five years now.
explanation: 'keep posted' = keep informed (idiom). Not standing as a guard.
explanationJa: 「keep posted」は「随時知らせて」。立ち番をする意味ではない。

sentences: Finishing this report by tomorrow is a tall order, honestly.
She placed a tall order at the cafe drive-through window on her way home from work yesterday.
Please bring a tall order of coffee to the office meeting room because everyone said they were thirsty.
He poured a tall order of orange juice for breakfast this morning before heading out to his early meeting.
explanation: 'a tall order' = difficult task (idiom). Not a beverage size.
explanationJa: 「a tall order」は「難題」。飲み物のサイズの意味ではない。

sentences: She served on the jury still out in the courtroom during the long trial last summer for two weeks.
Please report to the jury still out at the courthouse next Monday morning at nine o'clock sharp.
The jury is still out on whether the new policy will work.
He sat on the jury still out for nearly six weeks during the very famous murder trial last year.
explanation: 'the jury is still out' = undecided (idiom). Not a literal jury.
explanationJa: 「the jury is still out」は「まだ結論が出ていない」。実際の陪審員の意味ではない。
